official_excerpt.label: SSA’s single-month paid-versus-payable example
official_excerpt.text: We paid you $3,000 for June 2026. We should have paid you $1,500.

author: Shirshak J. Thapa, Benefits Letter Helper project
scope: Five text-evidence suggestions for initial Title II overpayment notices. Complete means all five measured elements are present in the example.
method: Three parent layouts, seven paired variants per layout. Annotation numbers count content lines below each page heading. All documents are constructed and none are claimant records.

families.basis: GN 02201.009 B.1, June 2026 single-month illustration. The period and paid/payable figures come from SSA. We supplied a fictional cause, administrative wording and rights.
GN 02201.009 B.1, the multi-period paid/payable chart. The three periods and their amounts are from SSA. The cause, surrounding words and rights are fictional.
Author-written wording challenge based on the required elements in GN 02201.009 B. All numbers and case facts in this family are invented.

cases.change: All five measured elements present
cases.text:
Page 1 of 2
Social Security retirement • training notice
The total overpayment is $1,500.
This happened because your earnings from work were above the retirement earnings limit.
The overpayment is for June 2026.
We paid $3,000 that month. The amount you should have received was $1,500.

Page 2 of 2
You may ask for reconsideration of this overpayment decision.
You may request a waiver of recovery.
Please refund the amount. Ask about installments or a different rate of withholding if you cannot repay it at once.

cases.change: All five measured elements present
cases.text:
Page 1 of 2
Social Security • training notice of overpayment
We calculated a total overpayment of $31,400.
You were overpaid because we did not apply your workers’ compensation offset.
These periods run from February 2023 through November 2025.
Feb 2023 to Nov 2023: we paid $1,000 a month and the correct payment was $500.
Dec 2023 to Nov 2024: we paid $1,500 a month and the correct payment was $600.
Dec 2024 to Nov 2025: we paid $2,000 a month and the correct payment was $700.

Page 2 of 2
You can appeal this decision in writing.
You can ask us to waive collection of the debt.
Please refund the debt. You can contact us about withholding or a smaller repayment rate.

cases.text:
Page 1 of 2
Social Security survivor benefit • training notice
Our total claim is $400.
Eligibility ended when your child left school.
The affected period is March 2026.
For that month you received $900. You were entitled to $500.

Page 2 of 2
You have the right to appeal the amount.
You may ask for a waiver.
Please repay the debt. Contact us about other recovery arrangements or a lower withholding rate.
